stem: How does the culture of adult medicine typically differ from paediatric medicine?

options.text: Adult medicine expects patients to function more independently
Adult medicine focuses more on growth and development
Adult medicine usually has better-supported multidisciplinary teams
Adult medicine usually involves greater parental involvement

explanation: Adult medicine expects patients to function more independently. In contrast with the family-centred paediatric model, adult services place more responsibility for care and attendance on the patient.
rationale: The key difference is who is expected to manage the illness and engage with care.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because adult medicine generally expects patients to take greater responsibility for their own care and attendance.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because paediatric care is the more family-centred model, while adult care is typically less so.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because growth and development are central concerns in paediatrics, not adult medicine.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the source indicates adult medicine is less likely to have multidisciplinary teams than paediatrics.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because parental involvement is a feature of paediatric care, whereas adult services expect more patient independence.

source.hint: Consider the difference in who is held responsible for managing the illness in each system.
